news.headline: President Trump pardons two Thanksgiving turkeys, Freedom and Feathers
news.summary: President Donald Trump held the annual White House turkey‑pardon ceremony, granting clemency to two birds named Freedom and Feathers. The turkeys arrived in Washington on Sunday after being raised on a West Virginia farm and will be retired after the event. The ceremony was livestreamed and attended by the first lady and other officials. The tradition dates back to the late 1940s and is a symbolic gesture each Thanksgiving.

news.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair linked to Chinese spy raises export‑control concerns
news.summary: U.S. officials say Jensen Huang, former Nvidia CEO, had a relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence operative, and that restricted AI chips may have been diverted to China during that time. The story has prompted Senate inquiries and statements from both Republican and Democratic lawmakers. President Trump and other Republicans have called for Huang’s reinstatement, while some left‑leaning outlets emphasize national‑security risks. The controversy highlights tensions over U.S. export controls on advanced semiconductor technology.

news.headline: Federal court unseals search warrant and documents in Ilhan Omar investigation
news.summary: A federal judge ordered the release of a partially redacted search warrant and related filings concerning the raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington, D.C., home. The documents indicate that prosecutors are examining alleged immigration‑related offenses dating back several decades. The release allows the public to see the scope of the Justice Department's inquiry. The case is being closely watched as it involves a sitting member of Congress.

news.headline: President Trump to award Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom
news.summary: President Donald Trump will present the Presidential Medal of Freedom to former New York City mayor Rudy Giuliani in an Oval Office ceremony. The award cites Giuliani's public service, including his leadership after the September 11 attacks, and his long‑time association with the president. The ceremony has attracted attention because the medal is the nation’s highest civilian honor and because Giuliani is a prominent political figure. The event underscores the political significance of the honor in the current administration.

news.headline: U.S. Army Reschedules Lead Azide Detonation at Iowa Ammunition Plant
news.summary: The U.S. Army announced that it will conduct a controlled detonation of more than 60 barrels of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The schedule change follows a federal court order that placed an indefinite pause on the operation and ongoing debate over public health and safety. President Trump has said the final decision will depend on court approval and the incoming Iowa governor. The Army says the timing is set to take advantage of optimal weather conditions.

news.headline: DOJ chief of staff warns staff of polygraph tests amid leak investigation
news.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche's chief of staff announced that Justice Department officials may be required to take polygraph examinations as part of an internal leak investigation. The announcement was made at a press conference where Blanche also briefed reporters on a large anti‑scam enforcement operation. The move has drawn attention from both political allies and critics of the administration. The DOJ also faced questions about a possible investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

news.headline: Pope Francis' private diary reveals visions of the devil and a spiritual crisis
news.summary: Excerpts from Pope Francis' personal diary, published by the Vatican, describe his experiences of seeing the devil and the "gates of hell" during a spiritual crisis in 2021-2022. The entries show the late pontiff grappling with demonic imagery amid concerns over the church's sexual abuse scandal. The publication has sparked debate over the relevance of the pope's private reflections to the public. The story highlights tensions between religious leadership and media coverage of personal faith experiences.

news.headline: California Gov. Gavin Newsom faces lawsuit over mass death‑row commutations
news.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the sentences of all 548 inmates on California's death row to life without parole. A coalition of district attorneys, law‑enforcement groups and victims' families has filed a petition with the state Supreme Court seeking to block the clemency, arguing procedural violations and lack of victim notice. The case pits the governor's executive clemency authority against prosecutors' claims of protecting victims' rights. The outcome could affect future use of mass commutations in other states.

news.headline: U.S. Army to Detonate Lead Azide at Iowa Ammunition Plant, Residents Evacuated
news.summary: The U.S. Army scheduled a controlled detonation of 68 drums of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on Friday. Residents in the projected plume path were asked to temporarily evacuate and schools were closed. Lawmakers and local officials have raised concerns about communication and potential health impacts. The operation aims to safely dispose of unstable explosives that could otherwise pose a safety risk.

news.headline: CIA unclassified intelligence network breached in cyberattack
news.summary: A cyber intrusion accessed an unclassified CIA system used for open-source intelligence analysis. The breach was discovered by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. No critical or classified capabilities were reported as disrupted. The incident adds to a series of recent hacks targeting U.S. government agencies.

satire.headline: Trump Announces Thanksgiving Turkey Won't Be Pardoned, Will Face Firing Squad
satire.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Donald Trump announced today that this year's Thanksgiving Turkey will not be pardoned and will instead face execution by a firing squad.
